title: Bitcoin Confirmations at Crypto Casinos in Canada
excerpt: Why does your crypto casino deposit wait for confirmations? Learn how block confirmations work, how many casinos need and what to do when a deposit is stuck.
author: David Andersen
bodyHtml:
You send crypto to a casino, the transaction shows as sent in your wallet, and yet the casino balance does not change. If this has happened to you, the reason is almost always blockchain confirmations. This guide explains what confirmations are, why casinos wait for them, how many are typical, and what Canadian players can do when a deposit seems stuck.

What is a confirmation?

When you send Bitcoin, your transaction is broadcast to the network and waits in a pool of unconfirmed transactions. Miners then group transactions into a block and add it to the chain. The moment your transaction appears in a block, it has one confirmation. Each additional block built on top adds another confirmation.

The reason this matters is security. A transaction with zero confirmations could still be replaced or dropped. A transaction with several confirmations becomes increasingly difficult to reverse, because someone would need to rewrite multiple blocks. Casinos want that certainty before they credit your balance, since crypto payments cannot be reversed once the casino has credited funds and the player has played them.

Why casinos require confirmations

A casino that credits a deposit too early takes on risk. If a transaction were later reversed or replaced, the casino could have paid out winnings against money it never received. Waiting for confirmations is how operators protect themselves, and it is a normal part of how a crypto casino works. We cover the broader point in our article on payment finality at crypto casinos.

How many confirmations are typical?

There is no universal number, and every casino sets its own rule, so always check the cashier page. As a general pattern, Bitcoin deposits are often credited after one to three confirmations, and some operators ask for more on larger amounts. Faster networks such as Litecoin or Solana usually need more blocks in terms of count, but each block arrives much more quickly. Stablecoins depend on the network they run on, which is why choosing the right chain matters. Our guide on which crypto Canadian casinos accept shows the options.

How long does a confirmation take?

Bitcoin blocks arrive on average about every ten minutes, but that is an average, not a promise. Some blocks come quickly and others take much longer. So one confirmation might take a few minutes, and three might take half an hour or more. If the network is busy and you paid a low fee, your transaction can sit unconfirmed for longer, because miners tend to prioritise transactions that pay higher fees.

This is why the fee you choose in your wallet matters. A very low fee saves a little money but can slow the whole process. Learn more in our piece on picking the right network and fee.

What to do when a deposit looks stuck

First, stay calm. A delayed deposit is usually a timing issue, not a lost payment. Work through these steps in order:

  • Find your transaction ID. Your wallet will show a hash or TXID for every transaction you send.
  • Look it up on a block explorer. A public explorer shows whether the transaction is unconfirmed or how many confirmations it has.
  • Check the address and network. Make sure you sent to the correct deposit address on the right network. Sending on the wrong chain can cause serious problems.
  • Check for a memo or tag. Some coins require an extra memo. Our guide to deposit addresses and memo tags explains this.
  • Wait for the casino's required count. If the explorer shows fewer confirmations than the casino needs, there is nothing wrong; you just have to wait.
  • Contact support. If the confirmations are complete and the balance has not updated, send support your TXID, the amount, the address and the time.

Never rush by resending

A common mistake is sending the deposit a second time because the first seems stuck. If both go through, you have deposited twice, and getting money back out of a crypto casino is not always simple. Be patient and confirm the first transaction's status before doing anything else.

Cashing out and confirmations

Confirmations also affect withdrawals, but in a different way. Once the casino sends your withdrawal, the same confirmation process applies on the network. The casino's internal review, any KYC checks and the network fee they choose will all affect how quickly you see funds. For tips on this, read our guide to crypto casino withdrawals.

Price movement while you wait

Crypto prices can move in the time it takes to confirm. If you send an amount and the price shifts before the casino credits it, the balance you receive is based on the value at the moment of crediting, according to the casino's rules. For anyone nervous about volatility, stablecoins can reduce that risk, though they have their own considerations. Our article on balances and price swings goes into detail, and you can learn the basics at our crypto gambling hub.

Keep records

Save every transaction ID, with date, amount and purpose. If a dispute arises, or if you need to report anything for tax reasons, good records save time. We offer a guide on record-keeping for crypto casino players. This is general information, not tax advice, so speak with a qualified professional about your situation.

A practical checklist

If you want to see how a specific operator handles crypto, our Neospin Casino review and the wider news archive are good starting points.

  • Check the casino's confirmation requirement before depositing.
  • Send a small test amount first if you are using a new address or network.
  • Pay a reasonable network fee so that your transaction is not left waiting.
  • Save the TXID right away.
  • Be patient and do not resend.

Confirmations are a small piece of the crypto experience, but understanding them removes much of the stress. As always, only gamble with money you can afford to lose, set limits before you play, and treat crypto balances like any other entertainment budget.
